name: Soulforge
reason: The source's unnamed 'mysterious furnace' floating in Luo Zheng's mind was given the evocative proper name 'Soulforge' to fit the Western fantasy register and to make the recurring artifact easier to track.
description: A mysterious furnace artifact that resides in Zane's mind, its surface etched with nine dragon-shaped sculptures (reliefs of nine dragons, including the Cobalt Dragon). Its inner fire can sustain or refine spirits, and it can emit beams of light and absorb treasures through the dragons' open mouths. It shares Zane's inner world with the nine True Dragons and the conscious sword spirit, and corresponds to the huge nine-dragon-relief furnace of the source novel.

name: Christopher
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Christopher' was chosen as a polished, respectable name fitting a prideful top-tier disciple.
description: A disciple regarded by Elder Howard as top-tier, exceptionally quick with Spatial Law for his age. During the obelisk trial (Eps 438-445) he quietly seethes as Zane clears nine obelisks in three days, eclipsing his own standing. Corresponds to Shuyue Kuang, the lower-realm ascender in the source's obelisk arc who had comprehended the Laws of Space and resented being outclimbed by Luo Zheng.

name: Divine-Class
reason: The source term 'Divine Artifact' was localized as the weapon grade 'Divine-Class' to fit the show's tiered weapon naming (Spirit Weapon, Mythic Weapon, Sacred Arms, Relic-Class).
description: The supreme weapon grade above Relic-Class, normally reserved for World Lords and Supreme Lords. The top Divine-Class weapons are ranked on the Cosmic Spirit Index, and the smith Delroy forged the Index's top ten. Distinct from the earlier tier-5 'Divine Arms'; corresponds to the source's Divine Artifacts, whose forging required the Upper Realm's cooperation.

name: Heavenly Destiny
reason: The source term 'Heaven's Will' was renamed 'Heavenly Destiny' to read more naturally as a bearable power in the Western fantasy register.
description: A supreme cosmic endowment that only beings at Supreme Lord level and above can bear; lesser cultivators cannot withstand it. It can be absorbed from a Crown (the Heavenly Will Crown of the source), a slow process, and its bearers can be sensed by other supreme powers. Corresponds to the source's Heaven's Will, whose rare appearance was known to only 128 Empyreans.

name: Thane
reason: The source character known only as 'Young Master Hao' was localized to 'Thane', a harsh single name suiting a towering Ogre warlord.
description: A towering, merciless Ogre warrior in the Illusion Battlefield arc (Eps 1202-1226) who forces weaker fighters to serve as his victims and harvests their points when they die. He wields a pair of axes that can split into countless blades and flow back into his hands. Corresponds to Young Master Hao, the ten-foot Demon Race youth with twin blood axes whom Luo Zheng confronts in the source battlefield city.

name: Martial Tournament
reason: The source's 'Martial Arts Conference/Competition' hosted by the World Business Alliance was tightened to 'Martial Tournament' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A decennial tournament hosted by the World Merchants' Guild in Oracle City, with the Dragon Soar Arena as the grand prize. There are no rules against killing, and non-sect fighters must pass pre-qualifying matches. It is the centerpiece of Eps 458-500 and corresponds to the Martial Arts Conference the World Business Alliance organizes in the source.

name: Crystal Martial House
reason: The source's Profound Jade (Black Jade) Martial House was renamed 'Crystal Martial House' to fit the Western register while keeping the gem-themed name.
description: A premier training institution of the Harlen Divine Kingdom, led by one head and two deputies who are seen as the kingdom's bedrock. Zane enters it to study and train during the Divine Kingdom arc (Eps 781-906). Corresponds to the source's Profound Jade / Black Jade Martial House of the Black Iron Divine Nation, one of the two great houses holding most of the nation's geniuses.

name: Axel
issues: Merged entity: the localized name 'Axel' was used for two different source characters - Xing Tiansu, the hammer-wielding imperial field commander (Eps 131-140), and Song Zhanpeng, Prince Ray's double-pupiled eyepatch fighter (Eps 341-342, source ch 328). These should be distinct characters.
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Axel' was chosen as a blunt, martial name fitting a hammer-wielding army commander.
description: Primarily the imperial army field commander at Silverspire (Eps 131-140) who wields hammers and fights alongside Yolande against the Dreadlords' forces, corresponding to Xing Tiansu, whose Quintessential Essence Avatar swings a huge sledgehammer in the source. The same localized name was reused in Eps 341-342 for a different character: one of Prince Ray's fighters, a large man whose eyepatched left eye hides double pupils that detect vulnerabilities (source: Song Zhanpeng).

name: Saint Viana
issues: Gender mismatch: episodes consistently treat Saint Viana as female ('her voice', 'her words', f8/m3), but the source counterpart Zhenren Tianqiong is male (m18/f0). The silver streak of light attack in Ep 172 matches the silver flash aimed at Zhenren Tianqiong in source ch 158, confirming the mapping.
reason: The source's Daoist title-name 'Zhenren Tianqiong' (Perfected Person Tianqiong) was localized as 'Saint Viana', converting the Daoist honorific into 'Saint' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A three-hundred-and-sixty-year-old Saint of the sect (Eps 171-285) who accuses and threatens Zane's side during the trial arc, striking Isla with harsh words, and is targeted by a silver streak of light shot from the ground. Corresponds to Zhenren Tianqiong of the Blue Cloud Sect, who tried to save Zhuge Feng and kill Luo Zheng at Admonition Mountain. The adaptation presents the character as a woman although the source character is a man.

name: World Tree
reason: Source term 'World Tree' was kept unchanged, as it already suits the Western fantasy setting.
description: A legendary tree whose Seed hangs at the top of a cave in the Illusory Battlefield arc (Eps 1142-1264), coveted by every warrior and Saint Lord present. Zane is lifted to it by a gentle updraft and swallows the Seed into his Sea of Chaos. Matches the source's World Tree Seed, which had hung above the underground palace for countless years without anyone obtaining it.

name: Bone Refining Level
reason: Source term 'Bone Refining Stage/Realm' was localized as 'Bone Refining Level', keeping the literal term while standardizing tier naming to 'Level'.
description: An early body-cultivation stage in which deep impurities are purged from the bones, roughly doubling a cultivator's strength; at its peak a fighter like Perrin strikes with nearly a thousand pounds of force. It sits below the Core Strength Level and corresponds directly to the source's Bone Refining Stage, the third of the five physical-body realms.

name: Melvin Lowell
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Melvin' was chosen for an earnest, unglamorous House member, with the surname 'Lowell' marking him as part of Zane's house.
description: A House Lowell disciple with innate natural strength that puts him on par with a Strength Level cultivator despite his low stage; early on he spars with Stone Golems and uses the Bull Rush Strike (Eps 5-12). By Ep 327 he has been demoted to a slave for breaking House rules and is used as a living punching bag by Miles and Darcy, yet remains defiant. Corresponds to Luo Dalong, the divinely strong Luo Family disciple who is later shackled as a 'human target' in the source.

name: Eagle Peak
reason: The source peak 'Xiao Yufeng' (Drizzling Rain Peak), one of the sect's 33 peaks, was renamed 'Eagle Peak' to fit the Western fantasy register alongside Misty Peak and Blackrock Peak.
description: One of the sect's peaks and Zane's home territory for inner disciples (Eps 39-200); its disciples fight alongside him against Demon Commanders in the forest and stand behind him when other peaks defect in Ep 126. The master sheet also notes it as the peak where Yates Moon trains. Corresponds to Xiao Yufeng, the Blue Cloud Sect peak Lin Geng and Luo Zheng are associated with in the source.

name: Demon Commander
reason: The source rank 'Demon/Daemon General' was localized as 'Demon Commander' to keep the demon hierarchy distinct in the Western fantasy register.
description: A mid-tier rank of demon appearing in dangerous numbers in the Sky Forest during Eps 116-144; encountering several in one day signals a far larger demon presence than estimated, and killing even two is a feat. Corresponds to the Daemon Generals that Blue Cloud Sect disciples face during the Monster Slaying Trial in the source.

name: Josef
reason: The unnamed Thearch Army general of the source was given the personal name 'Josef' so the adaptation's confrontation scene could use a named antagonist.
description: A military figure in the Silverspire/White Emperor City arc (Eps 124-126) who confronts Zane's group in the street, recognizes House Solomon tech, and furiously threatens Ingrid before being killed by Zane. Corresponds to the source's Thearch Army general who wields a Five-Clawed Golden Dragon of true essence and demands an explanation from Zhu Qianning for Zhuge Qingyun's death.

name: Gillwretch
reason: The source's generic 'fishmen' of the Fantasy Fish Pond were given the invented creature name 'Gillwretch' for a more vivid Western fantasy monster.
description: Fast, spear-throwing aquatic humanoids that guard Emberfin Lake's depths (Eps 179-200); their heads are their toughest feature, and they are actually sophisticated illusions projected by the magical array around the lake. They correspond to the fishmen conjured by the ancient Fantasy Formation around the source's Fantasy Fish Pond.

name: Holy City
reason: Source term 'Holy City' was kept unchanged for the Western fantasy setting.
description: The seat of the Saint Lord in the Upper Realm arc (Eps 1025-1123), a place so far above ordinary ambition that it does not even register as something to want. Zane is escorted there on the Saint Lord's direct orders by Masters Sloan and Hill. Corresponds to the source's Holy City of the Lingwu Holy Land, where the Holy Lord orders Luo Zheng to stay.

name: Divine Kingdom Continent
reason: Source term 'Divine Kingdom Continent' was kept unchanged, as it already suits the adaptation's setting.
description: The continent housing the Union of Seven Divine Kingdoms, setting of Eps 793-1084, visible alongside the Heartlands from high altitude. Zane underwent his Celestial Tribulation there and forged his body to Spirit Weapon level before moving on. Matches the source's Divine Kingdom Continent exactly.

name: Aether Crystal
reason: The source's 'Worldly Creation Pill', an ancestral cultivation elixir, was reimagined as the 'Aether Crystal' to match the show's crystal-based item vocabulary; it is canonically distinct from both the standalone 'Vitality' energy and 'Crystal Cubes'.
description: A rare cultivation aid and House Lowell family heirloom, of which the house owned only two; taking one radiates power and causes a cultivator's strength to skyrocket, as when Andrew stole and consumed the second crystal. Its theft from Zane is an early driving grievance (Eps 2-34), and its warming surge is referenced as late as Ep 1013. Corresponds to the source's Worldly Creation Pill, which only qualified young Luo Family disciples were permitted to use.

name: Hydra
reason: Source term 'Hydra' was kept unchanged, as it already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: A venomous multi-headed beast; its venom is renowned as its true weapon and forms the real challenge of the trial's third round (Eps 161-162), where Zane slaughters a pack of them. A giant sleeping Hydra statue also features in the later arc around Eps 1011-1137. Matches the source's Hydra from the trial tower's third level.

name: Shadow Phantom
issues: Master sheet misattribution: MasterLS credits the technique to Johanson (Eps 270+) and separately to Lewis Bailey (Eps 372-387), but episode usage shows the six Shadow Phantoms are Zane's own technique, deployed against Richard, Adrian, and Johanson himself; the source counterpart Heavenly Demon Phantom belongs to Luo Zheng.
reason: The source technique 'Heavenly Demon/Devil Phantom' was renamed 'Shadow Phantom' to avoid demonic connotations attaching to the protagonist's own skill.
description: A technique that conjures six identical dark combat duplicates used for attack and reconnaissance, prominent in Eps 257-374 against the Array of Thirteen Kills, Adrian, and Johanson. The wispy phantoms flicker when the user's dominion weakens but are far more powerful than they look. Corresponds to the source's Heavenly Demon Phantom, Luo Zheng's dark-purple vital-essence clones that automatically recondense when shattered.

name: Joe
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Joe Fane' echoes the source surname 'Fang' while reading as a plain Western name.
description: A fierce competitor in the Bloody Mountain trial (Eps 42-45) who fights Zane with a dagger and relentless calculated attacks. His Spirit Weapon creates near-unbreakable energy wire that can spread into a cutting net, leaving Zane covered in a web of cuts, a feat still remembered in Ep 261. Corresponds to Fang Yushu, whose sharp-thread net traps Luo Zheng at Blood Red Mountain in the source.

name: Owl Beast
reason: Source term 'Evil Owl Beast' was localized as 'Owl Beast', trimming the epithet for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A beast whose malevolent dead souls are imprisoned behind shackles (Eps 441-447); their ghosts exert crushing soul pressure, and Zane is told to devour them, finding the swarming spirits weaker than feared. The species recurs through Ep 829. Corresponds to the source's Evil Owl Beast from the same arc.

name: House Kincaid
reason: The source's Ji Family was localized as 'House Kincaid', following the show's convention of rendering clan surnames as Western noble houses.
description: One of the most powerful families in the Illusion Battlefield arc (Eps 1226-1289), supplying the local City Lord and sending ten thousand elite Soul Sea Realm warriors into the Battlefield alongside their champion. Their top talent is a woman who split herself into clones and will reveal her true power when they merge back into one. Corresponds to the source's Ji Family, whose prodigy Ji Luoxue fights through the Illusory Battlefield in cloned bodies.

name: Camilla
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Camilla' was chosen as an elegant but sharp name fitting a disdainful elite prodigy.
description: A contemptuous elite warrior on Lord Randy's team (Eps 797-869) who is ordered to spar with Zane and is known for going overboard, prompting Renzo's worry. She initially looks down on the newcomer and taunts him during training. Corresponds to Yue Ying, the aristocratic young lady of King Yan's team in the source who sparred with Luo Zheng while promising not to hurt him.

name: Lamar
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name; 'Lamar' was chosen as a heavy-sounding name fitting a hulking Ogre champion.
description: A tough Ogre powerhouse in the Tower of Sin arc (Eps 943-947) who wields a ghost staff that rates at best as a top-grade Relic-Class weapon. He survives Zane's three unheard-of projectiles with serious but non-lethal injuries, and onlookers assume anyone picking a fight with him is doomed. Corresponds to Mo Xiao, the Demon Race patriarch whose Ghost Head Staff is pierced by three black arrows in the source.

name: Emberfin Lake
reason: The source's 'Fantasy Fish Pond' (also translated 'Illusion Fish Deep Pool') was renamed 'Emberfin Lake' to match the adaptation's invented Emberfin fish and give the training ground an evocative Western name.
description: A Heavy Water training ground of the Skyreach Sect (Eps 179-188, referenced to Ep 961) where disciples must learn to move freely through the crushing water; access is managed by Steward Carter. Its hostile creatures are holograms projected by the intricate magical array surrounding the lake. Corresponds to the source's Fantasy Fish Pond, the heavy-water illusion formation where Luo Zheng trains.

name: Emberfin
reason: The source's 'Red Dace' fish were renamed 'Emberfins' to pair with the localized Emberfin Lake.
description: The agile fish of Emberfin Lake that slice effortlessly through the Heavy Water's turbulence and whirlpools; Zane learns to swim like one (Ep 180). Corresponds to the source's Red Dace, whose movements Luo Zheng studies in the Fantasy Fish Pond.
